judge_context: Two small, local edits: rename the kwargs in DatabaseWrapper.get_connection_params, and in DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env look up OPTIONS 'database' first, falling back to 'db' then NAME (mirroring the existing password/passwd/PASSWORD chain). Renaming the local variable to 'database' and keeping the nested .get() fallback style is consistent with the file; no new helpers or settings are needed.

case_items.name: Connection kwargs use non-deprecated names
case_items.name_zh: 连接参数改用非弃用名称
case_items.question: Does DatabaseWrapper.get_connection_params in django/db/backends/mysql/base.py now pass settings NAME and PASSWORD to mysqlclient as 'database' and 'password' instead of the deprecated 'db' and 'passwd'? (Not covered by hidden tests: the suite runs on SQLite.)

criteria.perfect: Both kwargs renamed to 'database' and 'password' in get_connection_params; nothing else in the kwargs building changed.
criteria.accept: Only one of the two kwargs renamed.
criteria.bad: base.py still emits 'db'/'passwd' (only dbshell changed), or kwargs are emitted under both names.

case_items.name: Deprecated OPTIONS keys remain supported
case_items.name_zh: 弃用的 OPTIONS 键仍被兼容
case_items.question: Do existing user configurations keep working: OPTIONS using 'db' / 'passwd' are still honoured by dbshell and still passed through to the connection, without raising the minimum mysqlclient version (both 'database' and 'password' are accepted since mysqlclient 1.3.8) or adding a hard error for the old keys?

criteria.perfect: Old keys still work as fallbacks; no version requirement change; at most a documented deprecation note.
criteria.accept: Old keys still work but the change adds noisy warnings or an unnecessary version check.
criteria.bad: Old 'db'/'passwd' OPTIONS stop working, raise an error, or the mysqlclient minimum version is bumped.
